name: Vesper-Sirocco

civilization.name: The Kessari Compact
civilization.notes: Steam-and-diesel engineers who survived the great drying by building continent-spanning canal cities; their aquifers are emptying faster than they can be replaced.

description: By day Vesper-Sirocco is a furnace of amber dust, its horizon a smear of ochre where dead ocean basins dissolve into dune fields taller than mountains. At dusk the wind reverses and the sirocco arrives, a scalding exhalation that drags walls of grit across canyon country and polishes the glass plains until they blaze.

The nights are brutally cold and utterly still, so quiet that travelers report hearing their own hearts. What sound there is comes from below: the groan of the canal city of Kessar Prime, its pumps and boilers beating like a failing pulse beneath streets built for ten million, now home to three.

Long before the Kessari raised their canals, something scorched half a hemisphere into glass, and their oldest scriptures name it simply 'the Second Sun.' The mining complex at Torvane Hollow was sealed a generation ago after crews broke into vaults of fused metal no one could cut or date; the orbital graveyard above holds satellites the Compact launched during its brief spaceflight era and can no longer reach.

Offworld buyers pay handsomely for helium-3 skimmed from the atmosphere, and the Compact sells it to keep its pumps running—selling, in effect, the air of its own decline. Every year the aquifers drop another meter, and every year more clans abandon the deep desert for the crowded canal cities. Something in those sealed vaults is still warm, and the Compact's last engineers know it.
